chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
When a woman sees blood before ten days (have elapsed), it is from the first menstruation (haydh); and if it was after the ten (days), it is from the next menstruation (haydh).

key_terms.الْحَيْضَةُ: haydh — menstruation; the specific blood of the menstrual cycle with distinct ritual purity implications
key_terms.الْمُسْتَقْبَلَة: al-mustaqbala — the upcoming/next menstruation; designating the blood as belonging to the following cycle
key_terms.عَشَرَة: ten days — the maximum duration of menstruation in Shia jurisprudence; blood before this limit belongs to the current cycle

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on blood seen before or after ten days of the menstrual cycle according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) addresses a key jurisprudential question concerning the classification of menstrual blood: if a woman sees blood before ten days have passed since the end of her previous menstruation, it is considered a continuation of the same menstrual cycle. If seen after ten days, it belongs to the next menstrual cycle. This ruling provides clarity for women observing ritual purity laws, particularly regarding when they may resume worship and marital relations.
